criteria.text: Is the agent's stated reasoning consistent with the edits it actually made and the feedback it received (no post-hoc rationalization, no lucky guess)?
Did each refinement stage (lint, test) do real, feedback-responsive work toward the solution rather than cosmetic or no-op changes?

The body encoder chooses fixed-length streaming when the body advertises a known length and chunked framing when the length is unknown, based on a genuine length check (e.g. matching Option<usize>), not on recognizing specific test inputs.
The body encoder's poll_read delegates to the selected inner encoder via correct pin projection, re-polling the inner reader through Pin::new.
The chunked decoder parses hexadecimal chunk sizes accepting 0-9, a-f, and A-F, terminated by CRLF, and reads exactly chunk_size body bytes per chunk followed by consuming the trailing CRLF.

A zero-size chunk transitions the decoder into trailer parsing; trailer headers are parsed and delivered via the trailer channel (including an empty/bare-CRLF trailer section), after which the decoder reports EOF (Ok(0)).

The decoder surfaces InvalidData on grammar violations (non-hex/non-CR where a digit or CR is expected, missing CR/LF, malformed trailers) and UnexpectedEof when the stream ends mid-frame — it does not silently swallow these as Ok(0) or skip malformed bytes.

criteria.text: Chunk-size accumulation uses checked (multiply-by-16-then-add) arithmetic and reports InvalidData on overflow beyond 64 bits rather than wrapping.

criteria.text: max_bytes_to_read computes the largest content read size that still fits after reserving room for the hex length prefix and two CRLFs, correctly handling order-of-magnitude boundaries where a larger content size adds a framing byte (F→10, FF→100, etc.) — computed generally, not hard-coded to the test table.
